import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Arnold–Givental conjecture and Arnold conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Arnold–Givental conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold%E2%80%93Givental_conjecture)
-/

open scoped Manifold
open CategoryTheory Filter Set

namespace ArnoldGiventalConjecture

universe u

variable {E M : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M]

local notation "𝓜" => 𝓘(ℝ, E)
local notation "𝓡" => 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ)

/-- The expression of a pointwise two-form in the extended chart based at `x`. -/
noncomputable def localTwoForm (ω : M → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ) (x : M) :
    E → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  fun y ↦ (ω ((extChartAt 𝓜 x).symm y)).compContinuousLinearMap
    (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓜 (extChartAt 𝓜 x).symm y)

/-- A smooth, closed, pointwise nondegenerate two-form on a smooth manifold. Smoothness and
closedness are expressed in every extended chart. -/
noncomputable def IsSymplecticForm [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M]
    (ω : M → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, ContDiffOn ℝ ⊤ (localTwoForm ω x) (extChartAt 𝓜 x).target) ∧
  (∀ x y, y ∈ (extChartAt 𝓜 x).target →
    extDerivWithin (localTwoForm ω x) (extChartAt 𝓜 x).target y = 0) ∧
  ∀ x v, (∀ w, ω x ![v, w] = 0) → v = 0

/-- Tangent vectors to a subset, represented by derivatives of smooth curves which locally stay
in the subset. -/
def tangentSet [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] (L : Set M) (x : M) : Set E :=
  {v | ∃ c : ℝ → M, ContMDiff 𝓡 𝓜 ⊤ c ∧ c 0 = x ∧
    (∀ᶠ t in nhds 0, c t ∈ L) ∧ mfderiv 𝓡 𝓜 c 0 1 = v}

/-- A subset is Lagrangian when each of its tangent spaces equals its symplectic orthogonal. -/
def IsLagrangian [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] (ω : M → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (L : Set M) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ L, ∀ w, w ∈ tangentSet L x ↔ ∀ v ∈ tangentSet L x, ω x ![w, v] = 0

/-- Two subsets meet transversely when their tangent spaces span the ambient tangent space at every
intersection point. -/
def IntersectsTransversely [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] (L L' : Set M) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ L ∩ L', ∀ v : E, ∃ v₁ ∈ tangentSet L x, ∃ v₂ ∈ tangentSet L' x, v = v₁ + v₂

/-- A diffeomorphism is an anti-symplectic involution if its square is the identity and its
pullback sends the symplectic form to its negative. -/
def IsAntiSymplecticInvolution [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M]
    (ω : M → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ) (τ : Diffeomorph 𝓜 𝓜 M M ⊤) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, τ (τ x) = x) ∧ ∀ x v w,
    ω (τ x) ![mfderiv 𝓜 𝓜 τ x v, mfderiv 𝓜 𝓜 τ x w] = -ω x ![v, w]

/-- A smooth isotopy of diffeomorphisms generated by a smooth time-dependent Hamiltonian. -/
def IsHamiltonianIsotopy [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M]
    (ω : M → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ) (Φ : ℝ → Diffeomorph 𝓜 𝓜 M M ⊤) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : ℝ × M → ℝ, ∃ X : ℝ × M → E,
    ContMDiff (ModelWithCorners.prod 𝓡 𝓜) 𝓡 ⊤ H ∧
    ContMDiff (ModelWithCorners.prod 𝓡 𝓜) 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⊤ X ∧
    ContMDiff (ModelWithCorners.prod 𝓡 𝓜) 𝓜 ⊤ (fun p : ℝ × M ↦ Φ p.1 p.2) ∧
    (∀ x, Φ 0 x = x) ∧
    (∀ t x v, ω x ![X (t, x), v] =
      mfderiv (ModelWithCorners.prod 𝓡 𝓜) 𝓡 H (t, x) (0, v)) ∧
    ∀ t x, mfderiv 𝓡 𝓜 (fun s ↦ Φ s x) t 1 = X (t, Φ t x)

/-- A Hamiltonian diffeomorphism is the time-one map of a time-dependent Hamiltonian flow. -/
def IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M]
    (ω : M → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ) (φ : Diffeomorph 𝓜 𝓜 M M ⊤) : Prop :=
  ∃ Φ : ℝ → Diffeomorph 𝓜 𝓜 M M ⊤, IsHamiltonianIsotopy ω Φ ∧ Φ 1 = φ

/-- The `i`-th Betti number with coefficients in `F`. -/
noncomputable def bettiNumber (F : Type u) [Field F] (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X]
    (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank F (((AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} F) i).obj
    (ModuleCat.of.{u, u} F F)).obj (TopCat.of X))

/-- The critical set of a smooth real-valued function on a manifold. -/
def criticalSet [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] (f : M → ℝ) : Set M :=
  {x | mfderiv 𝓜 𝓡 f x = 0}

/-- The minimum number of critical points among smooth real-valued functions with finitely many
critical points. -/
noncomputable def criticalPointNumber [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ f : M → ℝ, ContMDiff 𝓜 𝓡 ⊤ f ∧ (criticalSet (E := E) f).Finite ∧
    (criticalSet (E := E) f).ncard = k}

/-- A smooth function is Morse if the derivative of its differential is injective at every
critical point. At a critical point this derivative is the Hessian. -/
def IsMorseFunction [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] (f : M → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff 𝓜 𝓡 ⊤ f ∧ ∀ x ∈ criticalSet (E := E) f,
    let g : E → ℝ := fun y ↦ f ((extChartAt 𝓜 x).symm y)
    Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) (extChartAt 𝓜 x x))

/-- The minimum number of critical points among Morse functions. -/
noncomputable def morseNumber [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ f : M → ℝ, IsMorseFunction (E := E) f ∧ (criticalSet (E := E) f).Finite ∧
    (criticalSet (E := E) f).ncard = k}

/-- A diffeomorphism is nondegenerate when its graph is transverse to the diagonal, equivalently
when its derivative has no nonzero fixed vector at any fixed point. -/
def IsNondegenerate [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] (φ : Diffeomorph 𝓜 𝓜 M M ⊤) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, φ x = x → ∀ v, mfderiv 𝓜 𝓜 φ x v = v → v = 0

/-- **Arnold–Givental conjecture.** Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact symplectic manifold of
dimension $2n$, and let $L$ be a compact Lagrangian fixed-point set of an anti-symplectic
involution. If the time-one image of $L$ under a time-dependent Hamiltonian flow meets $L$
transversely, then
$\#(\varphi_1(L)\cap L)\geq\sum_{i=0}^n\dim H_i(L;\mathbb Z/2)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53 58]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.i [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] [CompactSpace M] [T2Space M]
    (n : ℕ) (hdim : Module.finrank ℝ E = 2 * n)
    (ω : M → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ) (hω : IsSymplecticForm ω)
    (L : Set M) (hLcompact : IsCompact L) (hL : IsLagrangian ω L)
    (τ : Diffeomorph 𝓜 𝓜 M M ⊤) (hτ : IsAntiSymplecticInvolution ω τ)
    (hfix : L = {x | τ x = x}) (Φ : ℝ → Diffeomorph 𝓜 𝓜 M M ⊤)
    (hΦ : IsHamiltonianIsotopy ω Φ)
    (htrans : IntersectsTransversely (E := E) (Φ 1 '' L) L) :
    (∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), bettiNumber (ULift.{u} (ZMod 2)) L i : Cardinal) ≤
      Cardinal.mk (↥((Φ 1 '' L) ∩ L)) := by
  sorry

/-- **Strong Arnold conjecture.** On a closed symplectic manifold, every Hamiltonian
diffeomorphism has at least as many fixed points as the minimum number of critical points of a
smooth real-valued function on the manifold. No nondegeneracy assumption is made.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53 58]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.ii [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] [CompactSpace M] [T2Space M]
    (ω : M → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ) (hω : IsSymplecticForm ω)
    (φ : Diffeomorph 𝓜 𝓜 M M ⊤) (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism ω φ) :
    (criticalPointNumber (E := E) (M := M) : Cardinal) ≤ Cardinal.mk (↥{x | φ x = x}) := by
  sorry

/-- **Nondegenerate strong Arnold conjecture.** If a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a closed
symplectic manifold has graph transverse to the diagonal, then its number of fixed points is at
least the Morse number, the minimum number of critical points of a Morse function.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53 58]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.nondegenerate_morse_number
    [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] [CompactSpace M] [T2Space M]
    (ω : M → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ) (hω : IsSymplecticForm ω)
    (φ : Diffeomorph 𝓜 𝓜 M M ⊤) (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism ω φ)
    (hnd : IsNondegenerate φ) :
    (morseNumber (E := E) (M := M) : Cardinal) ≤ Cardinal.mk (↥{x | φ x = x}) := by
  sorry

/-- **Weak Arnold conjecture.** For every field $F$, a nondegenerate Hamiltonian
diffeomorphism of a closed $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold has at least
$\sum_{i=0}^{2n}\dim_F H_i(M;F)$ fixed points.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 37 53 58]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.weak [IsManifold 𝓜 ⊤ M] [CompactSpace M] [T2Space M]
    (n : ℕ) (hdim : Module.finrank ℝ E = 2 * n)
    (ω : M → E [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ) (hω : IsSymplecticForm ω)
    (φ : Diffeomorph 𝓜 𝓜 M M ⊤) (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism ω φ)
    (hnd : IsNondegenerate φ) (F : Type u) [Field F] :
    (∑ i ∈ Finset.range (2 * n + 1), bettiNumber F M i : Cardinal) ≤
      Cardinal.mk (↥{x | φ x = x}) := by
  sorry

end ArnoldGiventalConjecture
modeling_decisions: The terse list-page entry is expanded using the linked Wikipedia article and Frauenfelder's formulation: part i uses a compact real Lagrangian fixed locus, an anti-symplectic involution, a time-dependent Hamiltonian flow, transverse intersection, and Z/2 coefficients.
Smooth manifolds are modeled as finite-dimensional boundaryless real Mathlib manifolds. `CompactSpace M` and `T2Space M` express that the ambient manifold is closed.
A symplectic form is represented pointwise on Mathlib tangent spaces. Smoothness and closedness are imposed in every extended chart, and nondegeneracy is imposed pointwise.

Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms are actual time-one maps of smooth isotopies satisfying both omega(X,-)=dH and the flow differential equation, rather than merely symplectic diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity.

The Hamiltonian family and flow are defined for real time. This implements the usual meaning of smooth data on [0,1] as restrictions of smooth data on a neighborhood; only the time-zero and time-one maps enter the conjectures.

Tangent spaces of subsets are modeled by velocities of local smooth curves. Lagrangian means equality with the symplectic orthogonal, and transverse intersection means that the two tangent spaces span the ambient tangent space.
The fixed-point and intersection counts use cardinal numbers so that the statements remain correct when a fixed-point set is infinite; finite Betti and Morse bounds are coerced to cardinals.

The strong Arnold conjecture's 'number of critical points of a smooth function' is read as the minimum over smooth functions. Restricting the defining set to functions with finite critical sets is equivalent on a closed smooth manifold because Morse functions with finitely many critical points exist, and avoids Mathlib's `Set.ncard = 0` convention for infinite sets.
A Morse function is defined by injectivity of its chart Hessian at every critical point. The Morse number is the minimum finite critical-set cardinality among such functions.
Nondegeneracy is stated by the equivalent condition that the derivative has no nonzero fixed vector at a fixed point, i.e. 1 is not an eigenvalue.
The weak variant quantifies over an arbitrary field parameter and is tagged `research solved`; its sum includes every degree from 0 through 2n.
For Z/2 coefficients in part i, `ULift (ZMod 2)` is used solely to align coefficient and manifold universes; it is the same coefficient field up to equivalence.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Arnold–Givental conjecture and Arnold conjecture

Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) symplectic manifold. A smooth family
$H_t \in C^\infty(M)$, $t \in [0, 1]$, of Hamiltonian functions determines Hamiltonian vector
fields $X_{H_t}$ by $\omega(X_{H_t}, \cdot) = dH_t$. The time-one map $\varphi_1$ of the flow of
$X_{H_t}$ is a *Hamiltonian diffeomorphism* of $M$. It is *nondegenerate* if its graph is
transverse to the diagonal of $M \times M$, i.e. $1$ is not an eigenvalue of $d\varphi_1(x)$ at
any fixed point $x$.

- **Strong Arnold conjecture.** Every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ has at least as many
  fixed points as the minimal number of critical points of a smooth function on $M$.
- **Nondegenerate variant.** Every nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ has at least
  $\mathrm{Morse}(M)$ fixed points, where $\mathrm{Morse}(M)$ is the minimal number of critical
  points of a Morse function on $M$.
- **Weak Arnold conjecture.** Every nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ has at least
  $\sum_{i=0}^{2n} \dim H_i(M; \mathbb{F})$ fixed points, for any field $\mathbb{F}$.
- **Arnold–Givental conjecture.** If $L = \mathrm{Fix}(\tau)$ is the fixed point set of an
  anti-symplectic involution $\tau$ of $M$ (so $L$ is a compact Lagrangian submanifold) and
  $\varphi_1(L)$ is transverse to $L$, then
  $\#(\varphi_1(L) \cap L) \ge \sum_{i=0}^{n} \dim H_i(L; \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$.

Symplectic forms are modelled as smooth sections of the bundle of bilinear forms on the tangent
spaces, as Mathlib does for Riemannian metrics. Closedness $d\omega = 0$ is expressed through the
invariant formula for the exterior derivative of a $2$-form in terms of Lie brackets of vector
fields. Betti numbers are ranks of Mathlib's singular homology.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Arnold–Givental conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold%E2%80%93Givental_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Fr04] U. Frauenfelder, *The Arnold–Givental conjecture and moment Floer homology*,
  Int. Math. Res. Not. 2004, [arXiv:math/0309373](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0309373)
- [RG17] G. Dimitroglou Rizell, R. Golovko, *The number of Hamiltonian fixed points on
  symplectically aspherical manifolds*, [arXiv:1609.04776](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.04776)
- [AB21] M. Abouzaid, A. J. Blumberg, *Arnold conjecture and Morava K-theory*,
  [arXiv:2103.01507](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.01507)
-/

namespace ArnoldGiventalConjecture

open scoped Manifold ContDiff Bundle
open Bundle Function VectorField AlgebraicTopology

section Definitions

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H}
  {M : Type} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [IsManifold I ∞ M]

variable (I) in
/-- A smooth vector field on `M`, i.e. a smooth section of the tangent bundle. -/
def IsSmoothVectorField (X : Π x : M, TangentSpace I x) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I I.tangent ∞ (fun x ↦ (X x : TangentBundle I M))

variable (I) in
/-- The value at `x` of the exterior derivative `dΩ(X, Y, Z)` of a `2`-form `Ω` on `M`, evaluated
on vector fields `X`, `Y`, `Z`, given by the invariant formula
$$d\Omega(X, Y, Z) = X(\Omega(Y, Z)) - Y(\Omega(X, Z)) + Z(\Omega(X, Y))
  - \Omega([X, Y], Z) + \Omega([X, Z], Y) - \Omega([Y, Z], X).$$
Here `X(f)` is the derivative of `f : M → ℝ` along `X`, and `[X, Y]` is the Lie bracket
`VectorField.mlieBracket`. -/
noncomputable def extDerivTwoForm
    (Ω : Π x : M, TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (X Y Z : Π x : M, TangentSpace I x) (x : M) : ℝ :=
  (show ℝ from mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) (fun y ↦ Ω y (Y y) (Z y)) x (X x))
    - (show ℝ from mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) (fun y ↦ Ω y (X y) (Z y)) x (Y x))
    + (show ℝ from mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) (fun y ↦ Ω y (X y) (Y y)) x (Z x))
    - Ω x (mlieBracket I X Y x) (Z x)
    + Ω x (mlieBracket I X Z x) (Y x)
    - Ω x (mlieBracket I Y Z x) (X x)

variable (I M) in
/-- A symplectic form on the manifold `M`: a smooth family `form x` of bilinear forms on the
tangent spaces `TangentSpace I x` (a smooth section of the bundle of bilinear forms, as for
Mathlib's `ContMDiffRiemannianMetric`) which is antisymmetric, nondegenerate and closed. -/
structure SymplecticForm where
  /-- The bilinear form `ω_x` on the tangent space at `x`. -/
  form (x : M) : TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ
  /-- `ω` depends smoothly on the base point. -/
  contMDiff : ContMDiff I (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) ∞
    (fun x ↦ TotalSpace.mk' (E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ) x (form x))
  /-- `ω` is antisymmetric. -/
  antisymm (x : M) (v w : TangentSpace I x) : form x v w = - form x w v
  /-- `ω` is nondegenerate. -/
  nondegenerate (x : M) (v : TangentSpace I x) : (∀ w, form x v w = 0) → v = 0
  /-- `ω` is closed: `dω(X, Y, Z) = 0` for all smooth vector fields `X`, `Y`, `Z`. -/
  closed (X Y Z : Π x : M, TangentSpace I x) (hX : IsSmoothVectorField I X)
    (hY : IsSmoothVectorField I Y) (hZ : IsSmoothVectorField I Z) (x : M) :
    extDerivTwoForm I form X Y Z x = 0

/-- `ψ : M → M` is a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of `(M, ω)`: there is a smooth family
`H t : M → ℝ` of Hamiltonian functions (smooth jointly in `(t, x)`), with Hamiltonian vector
fields `X t` defined by `ω (X t x) v = dH_t(x) v`, and a flow `φ` of the time-dependent vector
field `X` (that is, `φ 0 = id` and `∂_t φ t x = X t (φ t x)`), such that `ψ = φ 1` is the
time-one map. On a compact manifold the flow exists for all times, so this recovers the usual
notion. -/
def IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph (Ω : SymplecticForm I M) (ψ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (H : ℝ → M → ℝ) (X : ℝ → Π x : M, TangentSpace I x) (φ : ℝ → M → M),
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ).prod I) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ (uncurry H) ∧
    (∀ t x (v : TangentSpace I x), Ω.form x (X t x) v = mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) (H t) x v) ∧
    (∀ x, φ 0 x = x) ∧
    (∀ t x, HasMFDerivAt 𝓘(ℝ) I (fun s ↦ φ s x) t
      ((1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ).smulRight (X t (φ t x)))) ∧
    ψ = φ 1

variable (I) in
/-- A map `ψ : M → M` is nondegenerate if its graph intersects the diagonal of `M × M`
transversely, i.e. `1` is not an eigenvalue of `dψ x` at any fixed point `x` of `ψ`. -/
def IsNondegenerate (ψ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ fixedPoints ψ, ∀ v : TangentSpace I x, mfderiv I I ψ x v = v → v = 0

/-- `τ : M → M` is an anti-symplectic involution of `(M, ω)`: a smooth map with `τ ∘ τ = id`
(hence a diffeomorphism) and `τ^* ω = -ω`. -/
def IsAntiSymplecticInvolution (Ω : SymplecticForm I M) (τ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I I ∞ τ ∧ Involutive τ ∧
    ∀ x (v w : TangentSpace I x),
      Ω.form (τ x) (mfderiv I I τ x v) (mfderiv I I τ x w) = - Ω.form x v w

variable (I) in
/-- Let `L = Fix τ` be the fixed point set of an involution `τ` of `M`. Its tangent space at
`y ∈ L` is `T_y L = {a ∈ T_y M | dτ_y a = a}`. This predicate says that `ψ(L)` and `L`
intersect transversely: for every `x ∈ L` with `ψ x ∈ L`, the tangent space `T_{ψ x} M` is the
sum of `T_{ψ x} L` and `dψ_x (T_x L)`. -/
def TransverseImageFixedPoints (τ ψ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ fixedPoints τ, ψ x ∈ fixedPoints τ →
    ∀ w : TangentSpace I (ψ x), ∃ (a : TangentSpace I (ψ x)) (b : TangentSpace I x),
      mfderiv I I τ (ψ x) a = a ∧ mfderiv I I τ x b = b ∧ w = a + mfderiv I I ψ x b

/-- The `i`-th Betti number `dim_F H_i(X; F)` of a topological space `X` with coefficients in a
field `F`, computed with singular homology. -/
noncomputable def bettiNumber (F : Type) [Field F] (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (i : ℕ) :
    ℕ :=
  Module.finrank F
    (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat F) i).obj (ModuleCat.of F F)).obj (TopCat.of X))

variable (I) in
/-- The set of critical points of `f : M → ℝ`. -/
def criticalPoints (f : M → ℝ) : Set M :=
  {x | mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) f x = 0}

variable (I) in
/-- `f : M → ℝ` is a Morse function: it is smooth and its Hessian at every critical point `x`,
computed in the chart `extChartAt I x`, is nondegenerate. (At a critical point the Hessian does
not depend on the chart.) -/
def IsMorseFunction (f : M → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f ∧ ∀ x ∈ criticalPoints I f, ∀ v : E,
    fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm)) (extChartAt I x x) v = 0 → v = 0

variable (I M) in
/-- `Crit(M)`: the minimal number of critical points of a smooth function `M → ℝ`. -/
noncomputable def critNumber : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (f : M → ℝ) (_ : ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f), (criticalPoints I f).encard

variable (I M) in
/-- `Morse(M)`, the Morse number of `M`: the minimal number of critical points of a Morse
function `M → ℝ`. -/
noncomputable def morseNumber : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (f : M → ℝ) (_ : IsMorseFunction I f), (criticalPoints I f).encard

end Definitions

section Statements

/-
In the statements below, `M` is a closed symplectic manifold: a compact Hausdorff manifold
without boundary, modelled on the finite-dimensional real vector space `E` and equipped with a
symplectic form `Ω`.
-/

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  {M : Type} [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [CompactSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M]
  [IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ M]

/-- **Arnold–Givental conjecture.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a compact $2n$-dimensional symplectic
manifold and $\tau : M \to M$ an anti-symplectic involution ($\tau^*\omega = -\omega$,
$\tau^2 = \mathrm{id}$) whose fixed point set is the compact Lagrangian submanifold $L$. Let
$\varphi_1$ be the time-one map of the flow of a smooth family of Hamiltonian functions $H_t$,
$t \in [0, 1]$. If $\varphi_1(L)$ intersects $L$ transversely, then
$$\#(\varphi_1(L) \cap L) \ge \sum_{i=0}^{n} \dim H_i(L; \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}).$$

Here $L$ is `fixedPoints τ`; the fixed point set of an anti-symplectic involution of a compact
symplectic manifold is automatically a compact Lagrangian submanifold, with tangent space
$T_y L = \{a \in T_y M \mid d\tau_y a = a\}$, which is how transversality is expressed in
`TransverseImageFixedPoints`. -/

    (Ω : SymplecticForm 𝓘(ℝ, E) M) (τ : M → M) (hτ : IsAntiSymplecticInvolution Ω τ)
    (ψ : M → M) (hψ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω ψ)
    (htrans : TransverseImageFixedPoints 𝓘(ℝ, E) τ ψ) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), bettiNumber (ZMod 2) (fixedPoints τ) i ≤
      (ψ '' fixedPoints τ ∩ fixedPoints τ).encard := by
  sorry

fixed points of a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ is greater than or equal to the (minimal)
number of critical points of a smooth function on $M$. -/

theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.ii (Ω : SymplecticForm 𝓘(ℝ, E) M) (ψ : M → M)
    (hψ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω ψ) :
    critNumber 𝓘(ℝ, E) M ≤ (fixedPoints ψ).encard := by
  sorry

/-- **Arnold conjecture, nondegenerate form.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold.
A nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi$ of $M$ (one whose graph is transverse to the
diagonal of $M \times M$) has at least $\mathrm{Morse}(M)$ fixed points, where $\mathrm{Morse}(M)$,
the Morse number of $M$, is the minimal number of critical points of a Morse function on $M$. -/

theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.nondegenerate_morse_number
    (Ω : SymplecticForm 𝓘(ℝ, E) M) (ψ : M → M) (hψ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω ψ)
    (hnd : IsNondegenerate 𝓘(ℝ, E) ψ) :
    morseNumber 𝓘(ℝ, E) M ≤ (fixedPoints ψ).encard := by
  sorry

/-- **Weak Arnold conjecture.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed $2n$-dimensional symplectic
manifold and $\mathbb{F}$ a field. A nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi$ of $M$
satisfies

    (F : Type) [Field F] (Ω : SymplecticForm 𝓘(ℝ, E) M) (ψ : M → M)
    (hψ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω ψ) (hnd : IsNondegenerate 𝓘(ℝ, E) ψ) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (2 * n + 1), bettiNumber F M i ≤ (fixedPoints ψ).encard := by
  sorry

end Statements

attempts.decomposition_objections: None of substance. Note only that the notes for parts.i say 'compact' rather than 'closed'; I model M as compact and boundaryless (the only setting in which the conjecture is standardly stated, and the one used for the other slots), and that the 'Lagrangian submanifold' hypothesis in parts.i is a consequence of L = Fix(τ) rather than an independent assumption.
modeling_decisions: The list-page statement is a bare title; all four precise formulations were taken from the Wikipedia article 'Arnold conjecture' (Arnold–Givental section cross-checked against Frauenfelder arXiv:math/0309373, whose statement it matches verbatim).

Closed symplectic manifold = [CompactSpace M] [T2Space M] with ChartedSpace E M and IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ M for finite-dimensional E (model 𝓘(ℝ, E) means no boundary). Mathlib's IsManifold does not include Hausdorffness, so T2Space is added explicitly. Second countability follows from compactness.

M lives in universe Type (M : Type) so that singular homology with coefficients in ZMod 2 / an arbitrary field F : Type can be formed with ModuleCat.of without ULifts (Mathlib's ModuleCat.of requires the module and the ModuleCat universe to agree). Same convention as FormalConjectures/Millenium/Poincare.lean. In the weak conjecture, F ranges over fields in Type; Betti numbers depend only on char F so this loses nothing.

Symplectic form: smooth section of the bundle of bilinear forms on tangent spaces (mirrors Mathlib's ContMDiffRiemannianMetric), antisymmetric, nondegenerate, and closed. Closedness is the invariant formula for dΩ evaluated on all globally smooth vector fields; on a Hausdorff finite-dimensional manifold every tangent vector extends to a global smooth vector field (bump functions), so this is equivalent to dΩ = 0. Sign convention checked against VectorField.mlieBracket ([V,W] = D_V W − D_W V) and verified that constant forms on a vector space satisfy the condition.

Hamiltonian diffeomorphism: H : ℝ → M → ℝ smooth jointly in (t, x) on ℝ × M (the article's family on [0,1] extends to ℝ without changing φ_1), X t is characterised by ω(X t x, ·) = dH_t(x) (unique by nondegeneracy), φ is a flow of X for all t ∈ ℝ (exists globally on compact M), and ψ = φ 1. No separate diffeomorphism hypothesis on ψ, as it follows.

Fixed points and intersection points are counted with Set.encard in ℕ∞, so an infinite set of fixed points satisfies the bound (consistent with 'number of fixed points ≥ …'); using ncard would have been wrong (ncard of an infinite set is 0).

Strong Arnold conjecture: 'the number of critical points of a smooth function on M' is read as the minimum over all smooth functions (critNumber as an iInf in ℕ∞), as the notes require. Fixed points are all fixed points, not only contractible ones.
Nondegenerate: 1 is not an eigenvalue of dψ_x at fixed points (dψ v = v → v = 0), which in finite dimension is equivalent to transversality of the graph and the diagonal.

Morse function: nondegenerate Hessian expressed as the second fderiv of the local representative f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm at extChartAt I x x; at a critical point the Hessian is chart-independent. Morse number = infimum over Morse functions of the number of critical points.

Arnold–Givental: L is modelled as fixedPoints τ (the article says L is the fixed point set of τ). The hypotheses 'L is a compact Lagrangian submanifold' are not repeated, since the fixed point set of an anti-symplectic involution of a compact symplectic manifold is automatically a compact Lagrangian submanifold. Transversality of ψ(L) and L uses T_y L = {a | dτ_y a = a} and T_{ψ x} ψ(L) = dψ_x(T_x L), and requires their sum to be all of T_{ψ x} M. Coefficients are ZMod 2 and the sum runs over i = 0..n with finrank ℝ E = 2 * n, exactly as in the source.

Weak Arnold conjecture: sum runs over i = 0..2n with finrank ℝ E = 2 * n as in the source; tagged research solved per the decomposition notes (Fukaya–Ono, Liu–Tian, Ruan, Pardon over ℚ; Abouzaid–Blumberg over 𝔽_p).

  ∀ x : M,
    ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (coordinateTwoForm I form x) (chartAt E x).target ∧
      ∀ y ∈ (chartAt E x).target,
        extDerivWithin (coordinateTwoForm I form x) (chartAt E x).target y = 0

/-- A symplectic form is a smooth closed two-form which is nondegenerate at every point. -/
def IsSymplecticForm (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (form : TwoForm I M) : Prop :=
  IsSmoothClosedTwoForm I form ∧
    ∀ (x : M) (a : TangentSpace I x),
      (∀ b : TangentSpace I x, form x ![a, b] = 0) → a = 0

/-- The image of an embedded manifold is Lagrangian when the symplectic form restricts to zero. -/
def IsLagrangianEmbedding {EN : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup EN] [NormedSpace ℝ EN]
    {N : Type} [TopologicalSpace N] [ChartedSpace EN N]
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (J : ModelWithCorners ℝ EN EN)
    (form : TwoForm I M) (j : N → M) : Prop :=
  Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding J I ∞ j ∧
    ∀ (x : N) (a b : TangentSpace J x),
      form (j x) ![mfderiv J I j x a, mfderiv J I j x b] = 0

/-- A diffeomorphism is anti-symplectic if its pullback sends the form to its negative. -/
def IsAntiSymplectic (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (form : TwoForm I M)
    (τ : Diffeomorph I I M M ∞) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : M) (a b : TangentSpace I x),
    form (τ x) ![mfderiv I I τ x a, mfderiv I I τ x b] = -form x ![a, b]

/-- `φ` is generated by a smooth time-dependent Hamiltonian on the interval `[0,1]`. -/
def IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (form : TwoForm I M)
    (φ : Diffeomorph I I M M ∞) : Prop :=
  ∃ (H : ℝ → M → ℝ) (Φ : ℝ → Diffeomorph I I M M ∞)
      (X : ℝ → (x : M) → TangentSpace I x),
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod I) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ (fun p : ℝ × M ↦ H p.1 p.2) ∧
    Φ 0 = Diffeomorph.refl I M ∞ ∧ Φ 1 = φ ∧
    (∀ (t : ℝ) (x : M) (a : TangentSpace I x),
      form x ![X t x, a] = mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) (H t) x a) ∧
    ∀ (x : M) (t : ℝ), t ∈ Icc 0 1 →
      HasMFDerivWithinAt 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) I (fun s ↦ Φ s x) (Icc 0 1) t
        ((1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ).smulRight (X t (Φ t x)))

/-- Two parametrized submanifolds meet transversely if their tangent images span at every
intersection point. -/
def AreTransverse {E₁ E₂ : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [NormedSpace ℝ E₁]
    [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [NormedSpace ℝ E₂]
    {N₁ N₂ : Type} [TopologicalSpace N₁] [ChartedSpace E₁ N₁]
    [TopologicalSpace N₂] [ChartedSpace E₂ N₂]
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (J₁ : ModelWithCorners ℝ E₁ E₁)
    (J₂ : ModelWithCorners ℝ E₂ E₂) (f : N₁ → M) (g : N₂ → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x₁ : N₁) (x₂ : N₂), f x₁ = g x₂ →
    (mfderiv J₁ I f x₁).toLinearMap.range ⊔
      (mfderiv J₂ I g x₂).toLinearMap.range = ⊤

/-- The dimension of singular homology over a field. -/
noncomputable def bettiNumber (F : Type) [Field F] (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X]
    (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank F
    (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat F) i).obj (ModuleCat.of F F)).obj (TopCat.of X))

/-- A set has at least `k` elements if it is infinite or its finite cardinality is at least `k`.
This avoids the convention that `Set.ncard` is zero for infinite sets. -/
def HasAtLeast {X : Type} (s : Set X) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  s.Infinite ∨ k ≤ s.ncard

/-- The set of critical points of a smooth real-valued function on a manifold. -/
def criticalPoints (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (f : M → ℝ) : Set M :=
  {x | mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) f x = 0}

/-- The least number of critical points among smooth functions having finitely many critical
points. -/
noncomputable def smoothCriticalNumber (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (M : Type)
    [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | ∃ f : M → ℝ, ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ f ∧
    (criticalPoints I f).Finite ∧ (criticalPoints I f).ncard = k}

/-- A smooth function is Morse if the Hessian of its coordinate expression is injective at
every critical point. -/
def IsMorseFunction (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (f : M → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ f ∧ ∀ x ∈ criticalPoints I f,
    Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ (chartAt E x).symm)) ((chartAt E x) x))

/-- The Morse number is the least finite number of critical points of a Morse function. -/
noncomputable def morseNumber (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (M : Type)
    [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | ∃ f : M → ℝ, IsMorseFunction I f ∧
    (criticalPoints I f).Finite ∧ (criticalPoints I f).ncard = k}

/-- A diffeomorphism is nondegenerate when `1` is not an eigenvalue of its derivative at any
fixed point; equivalently, its graph is transverse to the diagonal. -/
def IsNondegenerate (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (φ : Diffeomorph I I M M ∞) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : M) (hx : φ x = x) (a : TangentSpace I x),
    mfderiv I I φ x a = hx.symm ▸ a → a = 0

/-- **Arnold–Givental conjecture.** Let $(M,ω)$ be a compact symplectic manifold of
dimension $2n$. Let the compact Lagrangian $L$ be the fixed-point set of an anti-symplectic
involution $τ$. If the time-one Hamiltonian image $φ(L)$ is transverse to $L$, then
$\#(φ(L)\cap L)\geq\sum_{i=0}^n\dim H_i(L;\mathbb Z/2)$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.i
    {EN : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup EN] [NormedSpace ℝ EN]
    {N : Type} [TopologicalSpace N] [ChartedSpace EN N]
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) (J : ModelWithCorners ℝ EN EN)
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ EN]
    [IsManifold I ∞ M] [BoundarylessManifold I M] [CompactSpace M]
    [IsManifold J ∞ N] [BoundarylessManifold J N] [CompactSpace N]
    (n : ℕ) (hdimM : Module.finrank ℝ E = 2 * n) (hdimN : Module.finrank ℝ EN = n)
    (form : TwoForm I M) (hform : IsSymplecticForm I form) (j : N → M)
    (hj : IsLagrangianEmbedding I J form j) (τ : Diffeomorph I I M M ∞)
    (hτanti : IsAntiSymplectic I form τ) (hτinv : τ.toEquiv.trans τ.toEquiv = Equiv.refl M)
    (hfix : range j = fixedPoints τ) (φ : Diffeomorph I I M M ∞)
    (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism I form φ)
    (htrans : AreTransverse I J J (φ ∘ j) j) :
    HasAtLeast (φ '' range j ∩ range j)
      (∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), bettiNumber (ZMod 2) N i) := by
  sorry

/-- **Strong Arnold conjecture.** Every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a closed symplectic
manifold, with no nondegeneracy assumption, has at least the minimum number of critical points
of a smooth real-valued function on the manifold. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.ii
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    [IsManifold I ∞ M] [BoundarylessManifold I M] [CompactSpace M]
    (form : TwoForm I M) (hform : IsSymplecticForm I form) (φ : Diffeomorph I I M M ∞)
    (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism I form φ) :
    HasAtLeast (fixedPoints φ) (smoothCriticalNumber I M) := by
  sorry

/-- **Nondegenerate Morse-number variant of the Arnold conjecture.** A nondegenerate
Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a closed symplectic manifold has at least the Morse number of the
manifold, the minimum number of critical points of a Morse function. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.nondegenerate_morse_number
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    [IsManifold I ∞ M] [BoundarylessManifold I M] [CompactSpace M]
    (form : TwoForm I M) (hform : IsSymplecticForm I form) (φ : Diffeomorph I I M M ∞)
    (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism I form φ) (hφnd : IsNondegenerate I φ) :
    HasAtLeast (fixedPoints φ) (morseNumber I M) := by
  sorry

/-- **Weak Arnold conjecture.** For every field $F$, a nondegenerate Hamiltonian
diffeomorphism of a closed symplectic $2n$-manifold has at least
$\sum_{i=0}^{2n}\dim_F H_i(M;F)$ fixed points. This homological form is now a theorem. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.weak
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    [IsManifold I ∞ M] [BoundarylessManifold I M] [CompactSpace M]
    (n : ℕ) (hdim : Module.finrank ℝ E = 2 * n)
    (form : TwoForm I M) (hform : IsSymplecticForm I form) (φ : Diffeomorph I I M M ∞)
    (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism I form φ) (hφnd : IsNondegenerate I φ) :
    ∀ (F : Type) [Field F],
      HasAtLeast (fixedPoints φ)
        (∑ i ∈ Finset.range (2 * n + 1), bettiNumber F M i) := by
  sorry

end ArnoldGiventalConjecture
modeling_decisions: The terse list-page entry was expanded using the linked Wikipedia article and the fixed decomposition: part i is the real-Lagrangian Arnold–Givental inequality, part ii is the strong Arnold conjecture, and the two requested generic/weak variants are separate declarations.

Manifolds are represented by finite-dimensional real model spaces with `IsManifold`, `BoundarylessManifold`, and `CompactSpace`. A compact Lagrangian is represented by a compact n-manifold embedded into the compact 2n-manifold; its image is required to equal the involution's fixed-point set.
A symplectic form is encoded as a smooth field of continuous alternating tangent two-forms. Closedness is defined chartwise using Mathlib's `extDerivWithin`, and pointwise nondegeneracy is explicit.

Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms are time-one maps of a family of diffeomorphisms satisfying the time-dependent Hamiltonian ODE on `[0,1]`, with the source's sign convention `ω(X_H, ·) = dH`. The Hamiltonian is represented by a globally smooth extension in time, while the flow equation is imposed only on `[0,1]`.
The anti-symplectic condition, involution equation, and equality of the embedded Lagrangian image with the involution's fixed-point set are separate explicit hypotheses.
Transversality is expressed by the sum of the two tangent-map ranges being the full ambient tangent space at every coincident pair of parametrized points.
Singular homology uses Mathlib's `singularHomologyFunctor` in `ModuleCat`; the degree sums are encoded by `Finset.range (n + 1)` and `Finset.range (2 * n + 1)`.

The strong conjecture's `Crit(M)` is the infimum in `ℕ` of finite critical-set cardinalities among smooth functions. The generic Morse number is defined analogously among Morse functions, with Morse nondegeneracy expressed by injectivity of the chart Hessian at each critical point.
The weak statement quantifies over every field `F`, as directed by the decomposition, and is tagged `research solved`; the other three declarations are tagged `research open`.
No contractibility restriction is imposed on fixed points, selecting the all-fixed-points reading in the decomposition.

Cardinality lower bounds use `HasAtLeast s k := s.Infinite ∨ k ≤ s.ncard`; this is necessary in the degenerate strong form because Mathlib's `Set.ncard` is zero for infinite sets, whereas an infinite fixed-point set certainly has at least every finite number of points.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Arnold–Givental conjecture and Arnold conjecture

Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$.
A smooth family of Hamiltonians $H_t \colon M \to \mathbb{R}$, $t \in [0, 1]$, generates the
Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{H_t}$, defined by $\omega(X_{H_t}, \cdot) = dH_t$, and their flow
$\varphi_t$. The time-one map $\varphi_1$ is called a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$.

* **Strong Arnold conjecture.** Every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ has at least as many
  fixed points as the minimal number of critical points of a smooth function on $M$.
* **Nondegenerate Arnold conjecture.** Every nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$
  (graph transverse to the diagonal) has at least as many fixed points as the Morse number of $M$,
  the minimal number of critical points of a Morse function on $M$.
* **Weak Arnold conjecture.** Every nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ has at least
  $\sum_{i=0}^{2n} \dim H_i(M; \mathbb{F})$ fixed points, for a field $\mathbb{F}$.
* **Arnold–Givental conjecture.** If $L \subset M$ is a compact Lagrangian submanifold which is
  the fixed point set of an anti-symplectic involution $\tau$ of $M$, and $\varphi_1(L)$
  intersects $L$ transversely, then
  $\#(\varphi_1(L) \cap L) \geq \sum_{i=0}^{n} \dim H_i(L; \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$.

Mathlib has no symplectic manifolds, so this file defines the needed notions. The manifold `M`
is modelled on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * n))` with the boundaryless model `𝓡 (2 * n)`, so
every tangent space `TangentSpace (𝓡 (2 * n)) x` is (definitionally) this model space. The
symplectic form is a family `σ x` of continuous alternating $2$-forms on the tangent spaces
(named `σ` rather than `ω`, since `ω` is notation for analytic smoothness). Smoothness and
closedness are required for the local representatives of `σ` in the charts of the atlas, using
`extDeriv` on the model space.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Arnold–Givental conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold%E2%80%93Givental_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Fr04] Frauenfelder, U., *The Arnold–Givental conjecture and moment Floer homology*,
  Int. Math. Res. Not. 2004, no. 42, 2179–2269. [arXiv:math/0309373](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0309373)
- [RG17] Rizell, G. D. and Golovko, R., *The number of Hamiltonian fixed points on symplectically
  aspherical manifolds*, Geom. Dedicata 190 (2017), 45–60.
  [arXiv:1609.04776](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.04776)
-/

section General

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H]

/-- The set of critical points of `f : M → ℝ`, i.e. the points where `df` vanishes. -/
def criticalPoints (f : M → ℝ) : Set M := {x | mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) f x = 0}

@[category test, AMS 58]
theorem criticalPoints_const (c : ℝ) : criticalPoints I (fun _ : M ↦ c) = Set.univ := by
  ext x
  simp [criticalPoints, mfderiv_const]

variable (M) in
/-- The minimal number of critical points of a smooth function `M → ℝ`, as an element
of `ℕ∞`. -/
noncomputable def critNumber : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ f : C^∞⟮I, M; 𝓘(ℝ), ℝ⟯, (criticalPoints I f).encard

/-- A smooth function `f : M → ℝ` on a boundaryless manifold is a Morse function if all its
critical points are nondegenerate: at a critical point `x`, the Hessian of `f`, computed in the
chart `extChartAt I x`, is a nondegenerate bilinear form. -/
def IsMorseFunction (f : M → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f ∧
  ∀ x ∈ criticalPoints I f, ∀ v : E,
    (∀ w, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 (f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm) (extChartAt I x x) ![v, w] = 0) →
      v = 0

variable (M) in
/-- The Morse number of `M`: the minimal number of critical points of a Morse function on `M`,
as an element of `ℕ∞`. -/
noncomputable def morseNumber : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ f ∈ {f : M → ℝ | IsMorseFunction I f}, (criticalPoints I f).encard

/-- A map `ψ : M → M` is nondegenerate if its graph is transverse to the diagonal of `M × M`,
i.e. `1` is not an eigenvalue of `dψ` at any fixed point of `ψ`. -/
def IsNondegenerate (ψ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, ψ x = x → ∀ v : TangentSpace I x, mfderiv I I ψ x v = v → v = 0

end General

/-- The `i`-th Betti number $\dim_{\mathbb{F}} H_i(X; \mathbb{F})$ of a topological space `X`
with coefficients in a field `F`, computed with singular homology. -/
noncomputable def bettiNumber (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (F : Type) [Field F] (i : ℕ) :
    ℕ :=
  Module.finrank F
    (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} F) i).obj (ModuleCat.of F F)).obj (TopCat.of X))

/- ### Symplectic forms and Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms -/

variable {n : ℕ} {M : Type} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * n))) M]
  (σ : ∀ x : M, TangentSpace (𝓡 (2 * n)) x [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ)

/-- The local representative of the family of $2$-forms `σ` in the chart `e`: the pullback of `σ`
along `e.symm`, a $2$-form on the model space `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * n))` whose values
outside `e.target` are junk. -/
noncomputable def chartRep (e : OpenPartialHomeomorph M (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * n))))
    (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * n))) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * n)) [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  (σ (e.symm y)).compContinuousLinearMap (mfderiv (𝓡 (2 * n)) (𝓡 (2 * n)) e.symm y)

/-- `σ` is a symplectic form on `M`: in every chart of the atlas its local representative is
smooth and closed ($d\sigma = 0$), and `σ` is nondegenerate on every tangent space. -/
def IsSymplecticForm : Prop :=
  (∀ e ∈ atlas (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * n))) M,
    ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (chartRep σ e) e.target) ∧
  (∀ e ∈ atlas (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * n))) M,
    ∀ y ∈ e.target, extDeriv (chartRep σ e) y = 0) ∧
  ∀ (x : M) (v : TangentSpace (𝓡 (2 * n)) x), (∀ w, σ x ![v, w] = 0) → v = 0

/-- `τ` is an anti-symplectic involution of `(M, σ)`: a smooth map with $\tau^2 = \mathrm{id}_M$
and $\tau^*\sigma = -\sigma$. -/
def IsAntiSymplecticInvolution (τ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff (𝓡 (2 * n)) (𝓡 (2 * n)) ∞ τ ∧ (∀ x, τ (τ x) = x) ∧
  ∀ (x : M) (u v : TangentSpace (𝓡 (2 * n)) x),
    σ (τ x) ![mfderiv (𝓡 (2 * n)) (𝓡 (2 * n)) τ x u,
      mfderiv (𝓡 (2 * n)) (𝓡 (2 * n)) τ x v] = -σ x ![u, v]

/-- `X` is the Hamiltonian vector field of `H` with respect to `σ`, i.e. $\sigma(X_H, \cdot) = dH$.
When `σ` is nondegenerate this determines `X` uniquely. -/
def IsHamiltonianVectorField (H : M → ℝ) (X : ∀ x : M, TangentSpace (𝓡 (2 * n)) x) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ (x : M) (v : TangentSpace (𝓡 (2 * n)) x),
    σ x ![X x, v] = mfderiv (𝓡 (2 * n)) 𝓘(ℝ) H x v

@[category test, AMS 37 53]
theorem isHamiltonianVectorField_const (c : ℝ) :
    IsHamiltonianVectorField σ (fun _ ↦ c) (fun _ ↦ 0) := by
  intro x v
  simp only [mfderiv_const, ContinuousLinearMap.zero_apply]
  exact (σ x).map_coord_zero 0 rfl

/-- `φ` is the flow of the time-dependent Hamiltonian `H`: `φ 0 = id` and, for every `x`,
the curve `t ↦ φ t x` is an integral curve of the time-dependent Hamiltonian vector field
`X (H t)`, i.e. `∂ₜ φ t x = X_{H t} (φ t x)`. -/
def IsHamiltonianFlow (H : ℝ → M → ℝ) (φ : ℝ → M → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ X : ℝ → ∀ x : M, TangentSpace (𝓡 (2 * n)) x,
    (∀ t, IsHamiltonianVectorField σ (H t) (X t)) ∧ φ 0 = id ∧
    ∀ (x : M) (t : ℝ), HasMFDerivAt 𝓘(ℝ) (𝓡 (2 * n)) (fun s ↦ φ s x) t
      ((1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ).smulRight (X t (φ t x)))

/-- `ψ` is a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of `(M, σ)`: the time-one map `φ 1` of the flow `φ` of a
time-dependent Hamiltonian `H : ℝ → M → ℝ` which is smooth as a function on `ℝ × M`. -/
def IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism (ψ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (H : ℝ → M → ℝ) (φ : ℝ → M → M),
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ).prod (𝓡 (2 * n))) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ (Function.uncurry H) ∧
    IsHamiltonianFlow σ H φ ∧ ψ = φ 1

variable {σ}

/- ### The conjectures -/

/-- **Arnold–Givental conjecture.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a compact $2n$-dimensional symplectic
manifold, let $L \subset M$ be a compact Lagrangian submanifold, and let $\tau \colon M \to M$ be
an anti-symplectic involution ($\tau^*\omega = -\omega$, $\tau^2 = \mathrm{id}_M$) whose fixed
point set is $L$. Let $\varphi_1$ be the time-one map of the flow generated by a smooth family
of Hamiltonians $H_t$, $t \in [0, 1]$. If $\varphi_1(L)$ intersects $L$ transversely, then
$$\#(\varphi_1(L) \cap L) \geq \sum_{i=0}^{n} \dim H_i(L; \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}).$$

Here $L$ is the image of a smooth embedding `ι : L → M` of a compact $n$-manifold on which `σ`
vanishes. Transversality is stated at every intersection point $p = \iota(a) = \varphi_1(\iota(b))$
as $T_p L + T_p \varphi_1(L) = T_p M$, where $T_p L$ and $T_p \varphi_1(L)$ are the images of
$d\iota_a$ and $d(\varphi_1 \circ \iota)_b$ in $T_p M = \mathbb{R}^{2n}$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.i [T2Space M] [CompactSpace M]
    [IsManifold (𝓡 (2 * n)) ∞ M] (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ)
    (L : Type) [TopologicalSpace L] [T2Space L] [CompactSpace L]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) L] [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ L]
    (ι : L → M) (hι : Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 n) (𝓡 (2 * n)) ∞ ι)
    (hι' : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) (𝓡 (2 * n)) ∞ ι)
    (hL : ∀ (a : L) (u v : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) a),
      σ (ι a) ![mfderiv (𝓡 n) (𝓡 (2 * n)) ι a u,
        mfderiv (𝓡 n) (𝓡 (2 * n)) ι a v] = 0)
    (τ : M → M) (hτ : IsAntiSymplecticInvolution σ τ) (hτL : {x | τ x = x} = Set.range ι)
    (ψ : M → M) (hψ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism σ ψ)
    (htrans : ∀ (a b : L), ι a = ψ (ι b) →
      (LinearMap.range (mfderiv (𝓡 n) (𝓡 (2 * n)) ι a).toLinearMap :
          Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * n)))) ⊔
        (LinearMap.range (mfderiv (𝓡 n) (𝓡 (2 * n)) (ψ ∘ ι) b).toLinearMap :
          Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * n)))) = ⊤) :
    ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), bettiNumber L (ZMod 2) i : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤
      (Set.range ι ∩ ψ '' Set.range ι).encard := by
  sorry

/-- **Strong Arnold conjecture.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold. The number
of fixed points of a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ is greater than or equal to the (minimal)
number of critical points of a smooth function on $M$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.ii [T2Space M] [CompactSpace M]
    [IsManifold (𝓡 (2 * n)) ∞ M] (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ)
    (ψ : M → M) (hψ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism σ ψ) :
    critNumber (𝓡 (2 * n)) M ≤ {x | ψ x = x}.encard := by
  sorry

/-- **Arnold conjecture, nondegenerate form.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold.
The number of fixed points of a nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ is at least the
Morse number of $M$, the minimal number of critical points of a Morse function on $M$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.nondegenerate_morse_number [T2Space M] [CompactSpace M]
    [IsManifold (𝓡 (2 * n)) ∞ M] (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ)
    (ψ : M → M) (hψ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism σ ψ)
    (hnd : IsNondegenerate (𝓡 (2 * n)) ψ) :
    morseNumber (𝓡 (2 * n)) M ≤ {x | ψ x = x}.encard := by
  sorry

/-- **Weak Arnold conjecture.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold
and let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field. A nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi$ of $M$
satisfies
$$\#\{\text{fixed points of } \varphi\} \geq \sum_{i=0}^{2n} \dim H_i(M; \mathbb{F}).$$
This is now a theorem: Floer (symplectically aspherical case), Fukaya–Ono, Liu–Tian, Ruan and
Pardon (fields of characteristic zero), and Abouzaid–Blumberg (finite fields). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.weak [T2Space M] [CompactSpace M]
    [IsManifold (𝓡 (2 * n)) ∞ M] (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ)
    (ψ : M → M) (hψ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorphism σ ψ)
    (hnd : IsNondegenerate (𝓡 (2 * n)) ψ) (F : Type) [Field F] :
    ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (2 * n + 1), bettiNumber M F i : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤
      {x | ψ x = x}.encard := by
  sorry

end ArnoldGiventalConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None substantive. Note only that the table's status 'open' applies to three slots; the weak Arnold conjecture is a theorem, and (following the table's own notes) it is tagged `research solved` in the file.
modeling_decisions: Mathlib has no symplectic manifolds or differential forms on manifolds, so a symplectic form is modelled as a family σ x of continuous alternating 2-forms on TangentSpace (𝓡 (2*n)) x (all definitionally the model space EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2*n))). Smoothness and closedness are imposed on the local representative chartRep σ e (pullback along e.symm via mfderiv) for every chart e of the atlas, using ContDiffOn and Mathlib's extDeriv on the model space; nondegeneracy is pointwise. Checking only atlas charts suffices since the atlas covers M and the conditions are chart-invariant.
The form is named σ (not ω) because ω is notation for analytic smoothness once `ContDiff` is opened; docstrings still use ω.

Closed manifold = [CompactSpace M] [T2Space M] with the boundaryless model 𝓡 (2*n) and [IsManifold (𝓡 (2*n)) ∞ M]; M : Type (universe 0) so TopCat.of M can be fed to the singular homology functor. Hausdorffness is added explicitly since Mathlib's IsManifold does not include it.

Hamiltonian vector field: σ x (X x, v) = dH_x v (the article's sign convention ω(X_H,·) = dH). Hamiltonian diffeomorphism: ψ = φ 1 where φ 0 = id and t ↦ φ t x satisfies HasMFDerivAt with velocity X (H t) (φ t x) (mirroring Mathlib's IsMIntegralCurve), for a Hamiltonian H : ℝ → M → ℝ smooth on ℝ × M. Time is taken in ℝ rather than [0,1]; any smooth family on [0,1] extends to ℝ, so the class of time-one maps is unchanged. The vector field X is existentially quantified and pinned down by the defining equation (σ nondegenerate); the flow is unique by ODE uniqueness, so no explicit diffeomorphism hypothesis on ψ is needed.

Fixed points and intersection points are counted with Set.encard in ℕ∞ (not ncard), so infinitely many fixed points (e.g. ψ = id) makes the inequality hold, matching the informal meaning; Set.ncard would return 0 and make the statement false.
critNumber I M = ⨅ over ContMDiffMaps f of encard (criticalPoints I f), i.e. the minimum over all smooth functions, as the notes demand. Critical point = mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) f x = 0.

Morse function: smooth, and at every critical point x the Hessian iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 (f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm) (extChartAt I x x) is nondegenerate (v ↦ Hess(v,·) injective). This is intrinsic at critical points of a boundaryless manifold; the definitions in the General section take an explicit model I so they can be reused.
Nondegeneracy of ψ (graph transverse to diagonal) is stated as: at every fixed point x, ker(dψ_x − id) = 0, which in finite dimension is equivalent to transversality.

Lagrangian submanifold L: a compact Hausdorff n-manifold L with a smooth embedding ι : L → M (Mathlib's Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding) such that σ vanishes on dι(T L). Since dim L = n, isotropic = Lagrangian. An additional (mathematically redundant) hypothesis ContMDiff ι is included because Mathlib has not yet proved that IsSmoothEmbedding implies ContMDiff; it does not change the class of admissible (L, ι).

Transversality of ψ(L) and L: for all a b with ι a = ψ (ι b) (i.e. every intersection point p, since ι is injective and ψ bijective), range(dι_a) ⊔ range(d(ψ∘ι)_b) = ⊤ as submodules of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2*n)). Both tangent spaces TangentSpace I (ι a) and TangentSpace I (ψ (ι b)) are E in the coordinates of chartAt at the same point p, so the type ascription is the correct identification.

Betti numbers: bettiNumber X F i = Module.finrank F of the i-th singular homology of TopCat.of X with coefficients ModuleCat.of F F (Mathlib's AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor). Sums run over Finset.range (n+1) resp. Finset.range (2*n+1), literally following the article; the field F in the weak conjecture is universally quantified over F : Type (Betti numbers only depend on char F, and every characteristic is realised in Type).

The *Arnold conjecture* bounds from below the number of fixed points of a Hamiltonian
diffeomorphism of a closed symplectic manifold $(M, ω)$ by Morse-theoretic invariants of $M$:

singular homology. Time-dependent Hamiltonians are taken to be smooth functions on `ℝ × M`; the

- [Wikipedia, Arnold–Givental conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold%E2%80%93Givental_conjecture)

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Arnold–Givental conjecture and Arnold conjecture

Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold. A smooth family of Hamiltonian functions
$H_t \in C^\infty(M)$ generates, by flowing along the Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{H_t}$
(defined by $\omega(X_{H_t}, \cdot) = dH_t$), a family of diffeomorphisms $\varphi_t$; the
time-one map $\varphi_1$ is called a *Hamiltonian diffeomorphism*.

* **Strong Arnold conjecture.** Every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ has at least as many
  fixed points as the minimal number of critical points of a smooth function on $M$.
* **Nondegenerate Arnold conjecture.** Every nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$
  has at least as many fixed points as the minimal number of critical points of a Morse
  function on $M$ (the Morse number of $M$).
* **Weak Arnold conjecture.** Every nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi$ of $M$
  satisfies $\#\mathrm{Fix}(\varphi) \geq \sum_{i=0}^{2n} \dim H_i(M; \mathbb{F})$ for a field
  $\mathbb{F}$. This version is now a theorem (Floer; Fukaya–Ono; Liu–Tian; Ruan; Pardon;
  Abouzaid–Blumberg).
* **Arnold–Givental conjecture.** If $L \subset M$ is the fixed point set of an anti-symplectic
  involution $\tau$ of $M$ and $\varphi_1(L)$ meets $L$ transversally, then
  $\#(\varphi_1(L) \cap L) \geq \sum_{i=0}^{n} \dim H_i(L; \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$.

Mathlib has no exterior derivative on manifolds, so a symplectic form is defined here as a smooth
antisymmetric nondegenerate bilinear form on the tangent bundle whose exterior derivative
vanishes, where $d\omega(X, Y, Z)$ is expanded through the invariant formula in terms of
Lie brackets of smooth vector fields.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Arnold–Givental conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold%E2%80%93Givental_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [U. Frauenfelder, *The Arnold–Givental conjecture and moment Floer homology*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0309373)
- [G. Dimitroglou Rizell, R. Golovko, *The number of Hamiltonian fixed points on symplectically
  aspherical manifolds*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.04776)
- [M. Abouzaid, A. J. Blumberg, *Arnold conjecture and Morava K-theory*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.01507)
-/

open scoped Manifold ContDiff Bundle EuclideanGeometry
open Bundle Set Function AlgebraicTopology

namespace ArnoldGiventalConjecture

/-- The `i`-th Betti number of a topological space `X` with coefficients in a field `F`, that is
$\dim_F H_i(X; F)$ for singular homology. -/
noncomputable def bettiNumber (F : Type) [Field F] (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank F
    (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat F) i).obj (ModuleCat.of F F)).obj (TopCat.of X))

section Definitions

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H]
  (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  [IsManifold I ∞ M]

/-- A vector field `X` on `M` is smooth if it is a `C^∞` section of the tangent bundle. -/
def IsSmoothVectorField (X : Π x : M, TangentSpace I x) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I I.tangent ∞ (fun x ↦ (X x : TangentBundle I M))

/-- The derivative `df_x(v)` of a function `f : M → ℝ` at `x` in the direction of the tangent
vector `v`, as a real number. -/
noncomputable def dirDeriv (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) (v : TangentSpace I x) : ℝ :=
  mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) f x v

variable (M) in
/-- A symplectic form on the manifold `M`: a smooth family `form x` of bilinear forms on the
tangent spaces `T_x M` that is antisymmetric, nondegenerate, and closed.

Closedness is expressed by the vanishing of the exterior derivative, expanded through the invariant
formula
$$d\omega(X, Y, Z) = X(\omega(Y, Z)) - Y(\omega(X, Z)) + Z(\omega(X, Y))
  - \omega([X, Y], Z) + \omega([X, Z], Y) - \omega([Y, Z], X)$$
for all smooth vector fields `X`, `Y`, `Z` on `M`. -/
structure SymplecticForm where
  /-- The bilinear form on the tangent space at `x`. -/
  form (x : M) : TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ
  /-- The form depends smoothly on the base point (as a section of the bundle of bilinear forms on
  the tangent bundle). -/
  contMDiff : ContMDiff I (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) ∞
    (fun x ↦ TotalSpace.mk' (E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ) x (form x))
  /-- The form is antisymmetric. -/
  antisymm (x : M) (v w : TangentSpace I x) : form x v w = - form x w v
  /-- The form is nondegenerate. -/
  nondegenerate (x : M) (v : TangentSpace I x) : (∀ w, form x v w = 0) → v = 0
  /-- The form is closed: `dω = 0`. -/
  closed (X Y Z : Π x : M, TangentSpace I x) (hX : IsSmoothVectorField I X)
      (hY : IsSmoothVectorField I Y) (hZ : IsSmoothVectorField I Z) (x : M) :
    dirDeriv I (fun y ↦ form y (Y y) (Z y)) x (X x)
      - dirDeriv I (fun y ↦ form y (X y) (Z y)) x (Y x)
      + dirDeriv I (fun y ↦ form y (X y) (Y y)) x (Z x)
      - form x (VectorField.mlieBracket I X Y x) (Z x)
      + form x (VectorField.mlieBracket I X Z x) (Y x)
      - form x (VectorField.mlieBracket I Y Z x) (X x) = 0

instance : CoeFun (SymplecticForm I M)
    (fun _ ↦ Π x : M, TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ) :=
  ⟨SymplecticForm.form⟩

variable {I} (Ω : SymplecticForm I M)

/-- `X` is the Hamiltonian vector field of the function `f : M → ℝ` with respect to the
symplectic form `Ω`, that is `Ω(X, ·) = df`. -/
def IsHamiltonianVectorField (f : M → ℝ) (X : Π x : M, TangentSpace I x) : Prop :=
  ∀ x v, Ω x (X x) v = mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) f x v

/-- `φ : M → M` is a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of `(M, Ω)`: there is a smooth family of Hamiltonian
functions `Ht t : M → ℝ` (`t : ℝ`) with Hamiltonian vector fields `X t`, such that `φ` is the
time-one map `ψ 1` of the flow `ψ` of the time-dependent vector field `X`, i.e. `ψ 0 = id` and
`∂ₜ ψ t x = X t (ψ t x)`.

Since `Ω` is nondegenerate, `X t` is determined by `Ht t`; since `X` is smooth, the flow `ψ` is
determined by `Ht` (and exists for all times when `M` is compact), so `φ` is the usual time-one
map of the Hamiltonian flow of the family `Ht`. The family is indexed by `t : ℝ` rather than
`t ∈ [0, 1]`; this gives the same class of time-one maps. -/
def IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph (φ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (Ht : ℝ → M → ℝ) (X : ℝ → Π x : M, TangentSpace I x) (ψ : ℝ → M → M),
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ).prod I) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ (uncurry Ht) ∧
    (∀ t, IsHamiltonianVectorField Ω (Ht t) (X t)) ∧
    (∀ x, ψ 0 x = x) ∧
    (∀ x t, HasMFDerivAt 𝓘(ℝ) I (fun s ↦ ψ s x) t
      ((1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ).smulRight (X t (ψ t x)))) ∧
    φ = ψ 1

variable (I)

/-- A diffeomorphism `φ : M → M` is nondegenerate if its graph is transverse to the diagonal of
`M × M`, i.e. if `1` is not an eigenvalue of `dφ_x` at any fixed point `x` of `φ`. -/
def IsNondegenerate (φ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ fixedPoints φ, ∀ v : TangentSpace I x, mfderiv I I φ x v = v → v = 0

/-- The set of critical points of a function `f : M → ℝ`, i.e. the points where `df` vanishes. -/
def criticalPoints (f : M → ℝ) : Set M := {x | mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) f x = 0}

variable (M) in
/-- `Crit(M)`: the minimal number of critical points of a smooth function `M → ℝ`. -/
noncomputable def critNumber : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (f : M → ℝ) (_ : ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f), (criticalPoints I f).encard

/-- A smooth function `f : M → ℝ` is a Morse function if all its critical points are nondegenerate,
i.e. at each critical point `x` the Hessian of `f` is a nondegenerate bilinear form. The Hessian is
computed in the chart `extChartAt I x` at `x`; at a critical point (in the interior of `M`) it does
not depend on the choice of chart. -/
def IsMorseFunction (f : M → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f ∧
  ∀ x ∈ criticalPoints I f, ∀ v : E,
    (∀ w, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm)) (extChartAt I x x) v w = 0) → v = 0

variable (M) in
/-- `Morse(M)`, the Morse number of `M`: the minimal number of critical points of a Morse function
`M → ℝ`. -/
noncomputable def morseNumber : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (f : M → ℝ) (_ : IsMorseFunction I f), (criticalPoints I f).encard

variable {I}

/-- `τ : M → M` is an anti-symplectic involution of `(M, Ω)`: a smooth map with `τ ∘ τ = id` and
`τ^* Ω = -Ω`. -/
def IsAntiSymplecticInvolution (τ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I I ∞ τ ∧ τ ∘ τ = id ∧
  ∀ x (v w : TangentSpace I x), Ω (τ x) (mfderiv I I τ x v) (mfderiv I I τ x w) = - Ω x v w

variable (I)

/-- For `τ` a smooth involution of `M` with fixed point set `L` and `φ` a diffeomorphism of `M`,
`φ(L)` intersects `L` transversally: at every point `x = φ y` of `φ(L) ∩ L` (with `y ∈ L`) one has
`T_x φ(L) + T_x L = T_x M`, where `T_x L = {a | dτ_x a = a}` is the tangent space of the fixed point
set of the involution `τ` and `T_x φ(L) = dφ_y (T_y L)`. -/
def IsTransverseToFixedPoints (τ φ : M → M) : Prop :=
  ∀ y ∈ fixedPoints τ, φ y ∈ fixedPoints τ →
    ∀ u : TangentSpace I (φ y), ∃ (a : TangentSpace I (φ y)) (b : TangentSpace I y),
      mfderiv I I τ (φ y) a = a ∧ mfderiv I I τ y b = b ∧ u = a + mfderiv I I φ y b

end Definitions

section Tests

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H]
  {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  [IsManifold I ∞ M] (Ω : SymplecticForm I M)

/-- A symplectic form vanishes on pairs of equal vectors. -/
@[category API, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem SymplecticForm.apply_self (x : M) (v : TangentSpace I x) : Ω x v v = 0 := by
  have := Ω.antisymm x v v
  linarith

/-- The identity is a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism (generated by the zero Hamiltonian). -/
@[category test, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem isHamiltonianDiffeomorph_id : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω id := by
  refine ⟨fun _ _ ↦ 0, fun _ _ ↦ 0, fun _ x ↦ x, contMDiff_const, ?_, fun _ ↦ rfl, ?_, rfl⟩
  · intro t x v
    simp [mfderiv_const]
  · intro x t
    have : (1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ).smulRight (0 : TangentSpace I x) = 0 := by ext; simp
    rw [this]
    exact hasMFDerivAt_const x t

omit [IsManifold I ∞ M] in
/-- The identity is not nondegenerate on a nonempty manifold modelled on a nontrivial space. -/
@[category test, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem not_isNondegenerate_id [Nonempty M] [Nontrivial E] : ¬ IsNondegenerate I (id : M → M) := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨x⟩ := ‹Nonempty M›
  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := exists_ne (0 : E)
  exact hv (h x rfl v (by simp))

end Tests

section Conjectures

variable {n : ℕ} {M : Type} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (ℝ^(2 * n)) M]
  [IsManifold (𝓡 (2 * n)) ∞ M] [CompactSpace M] [T2Space M] (Ω : SymplecticForm (𝓡 (2 * n)) M)

/-- **Arnold–Givental conjecture.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a compact $2n$-dimensional symplectic
manifold and let $\tau : M \to M$ be an anti-symplectic involution ($\tau^*\omega = -\omega$,
$\tau^2 = \mathrm{id}$) with fixed point set $L$ (which is then a compact Lagrangian submanifold
of $M$). Let $H_t \in C^\infty(M)$, $t \in [0, 1]$, be a smooth family of Hamiltonian functions
generating the Hamiltonian flow $\varphi_t$. If $\varphi_1(L)$ intersects $L$ transversally, then
$$\#(\varphi_1(L) \cap L) \geq \sum_{i=0}^{n} \dim H_i(L; \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}).$$ -/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.i (τ φ : M → M) (hτ : IsAntiSymplecticInvolution Ω τ)
    (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω φ) (hL : IsTransverseToFixedPoints (𝓡 (2 * n)) τ φ) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), bettiNumber (ZMod 2) (fixedPoints τ) i ≤
      (φ '' fixedPoints τ ∩ fixedPoints τ).encard := by
  sorry

fixed points of any Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ is at least the number of critical points of
a smooth function on $M$, i.e. at least
$$\mathrm{Crit}(M) = \min \{ \#\mathrm{Crit}(f) : f \in C^\infty(M, \mathbb{R}) \}.$$ -/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.ii (φ : M → M) (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω φ) :
    critNumber (𝓡 (2 * n)) M ≤ (fixedPoints φ).encard := by
  sorry

/-- **Arnold conjecture, nondegenerate case.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold.
The number of fixed points of any nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ (one whose graph
is transverse to the diagonal of $M \times M$) is at least the Morse number of $M$, the minimal
number of critical points of a Morse function on $M$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.nondegenerate_morse_number (φ : M → M)
    (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω φ) (hnd : IsNondegenerate (𝓡 (2 * n)) φ) :
    morseNumber (𝓡 (2 * n)) M ≤ (fixedPoints φ).encard := by
  sorry

/-- **Weak Arnold conjecture.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold
and let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field. For every nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism
$\varphi : M \to M$,
$$\#\{\text{fixed points of } \varphi\} \geq \sum_{i=0}^{2n} \dim H_i(M; \mathbb{F}).$$

@[category research solved, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.weak (F : Type) [Field F] (φ : M → M)
    (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω φ) (hnd : IsNondegenerate (𝓡 (2 * n)) φ) :

end Conjectures

end ArnoldGiventalConjecture

modeling_decisions: Closed manifold = [CompactSpace M] [T2Space M] with model 𝓡 (2 * n) (boundaryless, dimension 2n). Universe fixed to M : Type (as in the repo's Poincaré file) so that singular homology with coefficients in ModuleCat F (F : Type) typechecks.

Symplectic form (bespoke `SymplecticForm I M`): a C^∞ section x ↦ form x of the bundle of continuous bilinear forms on TM (same encoding as Mathlib's ContMDiffRiemannianMetric), antisymmetric, nondegenerate, and closed. Mathlib has no exterior derivative on manifolds, so dω = 0 is expressed via the invariant formula dω(X,Y,Z) = X ω(Y,Z) − Y ω(X,Z) + Z ω(X,Y) − ω([X,Y],Z) + ω([X,Z],Y) − ω([Y,Z],X) = 0 for all smooth vector fields X,Y,Z, using VectorField.mlieBracket (whose sign convention [V,W] = DW·V − DV·W is the standard one, so the formula is exactly dω). On compact Hausdorff manifolds every tangent vector extends to a global smooth vector field, so this is equivalent to dω = 0. Directional derivatives are wrapped in `dirDeriv` (returns ℝ) because `mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) f x v : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ) _` does not elaborate under +/-.

Hamiltonian vector field: ω(X_H, ·) = dH (the article's sign convention). Hamiltonian diffeomorphism: ∃ smooth Ht : ℝ × M → ℝ, X t Hamiltonian for Ht t, and ψ : ℝ → M → M with ψ 0 = id and HasMFDerivAt of t ↦ ψ t x equal to X t (ψ t x) (Mathlib's IsMIntegralCurve encoding), φ = ψ 1. No smoothness/diffeomorphism property of ψ is imposed: by nondegeneracy X is determined by Ht and by ODE uniqueness ψ is the flow, so φ is exactly the time-one map. The family is indexed by ℝ instead of [0,1]; this yields the same class of time-one maps.

Nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism: ∀ fixed point x, ∀ v, dφ_x v = v → v = 0 (1 is not an eigenvalue of dφ_x), which is equivalent to the article's 'graph transverse to the diagonal'. Since φ x = x, mfderiv I I φ x is computed in the single chart at x, so the eigenvalue condition is chart-independent.

Crit(M) is read as the minimum over all smooth f : M → ℝ of the number of critical points ({x | mfderiv f x = 0}), as the table prescribes; counted with Set.encard in ℕ∞ and iInf over smooth f. Morse(M) likewise over Morse functions. A Morse function is smooth with nondegenerate Hessian at every critical point; the Hessian is the second fderiv of f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm at extChartAt I x x, which at critical points (interior, boundaryless model) is chart-independent up to linear isomorphism, so nondegeneracy is well defined.

Arnold–Givental: L is taken to be fixedPoints τ for τ an anti-symplectic involution (smooth, τ ∘ τ = id, ω_{τx}(dτ v, dτ w) = −ω_x(v,w)). The article's separate hypothesis 'L compact Lagrangian submanifold' is automatic (Fix τ is closed in compact M, and the fixed point set of an anti-symplectic involution is Lagrangian), so it is not repeated. Transversality φ(L) ⋔ L is encoded as: for all y ∈ L with φ y ∈ L, every u ∈ T_{φ y}M is a + dφ_y b with dτ_{φ y} a = a and dτ_y b = b, using T_x Fix(τ) = ker(dτ_x − id) (true for smooth involutions) and T_{φ y} φ(L) = dφ_y(T_y L). Intersection count is encard (φ '' L ∩ L) in ℕ∞ (finite under transversality).

Betti numbers: bettiNumber F X i := Module.finrank F of the i-th singular homology of TopCat.of X with coefficients in ModuleCat.of F F (AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor). Sums run over Finset.range (n+1) (for L) and Finset.range (2n+1) (for M) as in the article; the weak conjecture quantifies over all fields F : Type.

All fixed points are counted in the Arnold conjecture statements (the article does not restrict to contractible ones). Category tags follow the task: parts.i, parts.ii and the Morse-number variant are research open; the weak (homological) variant is research solved. AMS 37 53 57.

Two small test/API theorems with proofs are included (identity is a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism; identity is not nondegenerate on a nonempty manifold with nontrivial model space; ω(v,v) = 0) to sanity-check the bespoke definitions.

arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.i.why: Stated for a compact T2 manifold M modelled on ℝ^(2n) with a bespoke SymplecticForm, an anti-symplectic involution τ (smooth, τ∘τ=id, τ*ω=-ω) with L := fixedPoints τ, a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism φ (time-one map of the flow of a smooth time-dependent Hamiltonian), transversality of φ(L) and L expressed via tangent spaces, and the bound ∑_{i=0}^{n} dim H_i(L; ZMod 2) ≤ encard (φ '' L ∩ L) using Mathlib's singular homology.

arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.ii.why: Strong Arnold conjecture: for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism φ of a closed symplectic manifold, critNumber M (the infimum over smooth f : M → ℝ of the encard of {x | mfderiv f x = 0}) ≤ encard (fixedPoints φ). All fixed points are counted, as in the article.

arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.nond.why: For φ Hamiltonian and nondegenerate (1 not an eigenvalue of dφ_x at fixed points, equivalent to graph ⋔ diagonal), morseNumber M ≤ encard (fixedPoints φ), where morseNumber is the infimum of the number of critical points over Morse functions (smooth, with nondegenerate chart Hessian at each critical point).

arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.weak.why: For every field F and nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism φ, ∑_{i=0}^{2n} dim H_i(M; F) ≤ encard (fixedPoints φ); tagged research solved per the table (Floer, Fukaya–Ono, Liu–Tian, Ruan, Pardon, Abouzaid–Blumberg).

statement_blocks.arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.i:
/-- **Arnold–Givental conjecture.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a compact $2n$-dimensional symplectic
manifold and let $\tau : M \to M$ be an anti-symplectic involution ($\tau^*\omega = -\omega$,
$\tau^2 = \mathrm{id}$) with fixed point set $L$ (which is then a compact Lagrangian submanifold
of $M$). Let $H_t \in C^\infty(M)$, $t \in [0, 1]$, be a smooth family of Hamiltonian functions
generating the Hamiltonian flow $\varphi_t$. If $\varphi_1(L)$ intersects $L$ transversally, then
$$\#(\varphi_1(L) \cap L) \geq \sum_{i=0}^{n} \dim H_i(L; \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}).$$ -/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.i (τ φ : M → M) (hτ : IsAntiSymplecticInvolution Ω τ)
    (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω φ) (hL : IsTransverseToFixedPoints (𝓡 (2 * n)) τ φ) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), bettiNumber (ZMod 2) (fixedPoints τ) i ≤
      (φ '' fixedPoints τ ∩ fixedPoints τ).encard := by
  sorry
statement_blocks.arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.ii:
/-- **Strong Arnold conjecture.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold. The number of
fixed points of any Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ is at least the number of critical points of
a smooth function on $M$, i.e. at least
$$\mathrm{Crit}(M) = \min \{ \#\mathrm{Crit}(f) : f \in C^\infty(M, \mathbb{R}) \}.$$ -/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.parts.ii (φ : M → M) (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω φ) :
    critNumber (𝓡 (2 * n)) M ≤ (fixedPoints φ).encard := by
  sorry
statement_blocks.arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.nond:
/-- **Arnold conjecture, nondegenerate case.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold.
The number of fixed points of any nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of $M$ (one whose graph
is transverse to the diagonal of $M \times M$) is at least the Morse number of $M$, the minimal
number of critical points of a Morse function on $M$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.nondegenerate_morse_number (φ : M → M)
    (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω φ) (hnd : IsNondegenerate (𝓡 (2 * n)) φ) :
    morseNumber (𝓡 (2 * n)) M ≤ (fixedPoints φ).encard := by
  sorry
statement_blocks.arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.weak:
/-- **Weak Arnold conjecture.** Let $(M, \omega)$ be a closed $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold
and let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field. For every nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism
$\varphi : M \to M$,
$$\#\{\text{fixed points of } \varphi\} \geq \sum_{i=0}^{2n} \dim H_i(M; \mathbb{F}).$$
This is now a theorem: Floer (symplectically aspherical case), Fukaya–Ono, Liu–Tian, Ruan and
Pardon (characteristic zero), Abouzaid–Blumberg (finite characteristic). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 37 53 57]
theorem arnold_givental_conjecture.variants.weak (F : Type) [Field F] (φ : M → M)
    (hφ : IsHamiltonianDiffeomorph Ω φ) (hnd : IsNondegenerate (𝓡 (2 * n)) φ) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (2 * n + 1), bettiNumber F M i ≤ (fixedPoints φ).encard := by
  sorry
